root_cause: Interface Fa0/2 is assigned to VLAN 20 instead of the required VLAN 10.
evidence: show vlan brief shows VLAN 10 exists | show interfaces switchport shows Fa0/2 is assigned to VLAN 20
fix_steps: configure terminal | interface Fa0/2 | switchport access vlan 10 | end
additional_evidence_needed: Confirmation of PC-A port assignment via show mac address-table or show interfaces switchport for Fa0/1.
risk: Low - reassigning the access VLAN on interface Fa0/2 will briefly disrupt network traffic on that port as it switches to VLAN 10.
expected_fault: Fa0/2 is assigned to the wrong VLAN.
human_correction: Confirmed Fa0/2 must be assigned to VLAN 10.
reason_for_correction: Compared AI diagnosis with the documented expected fault and available network evidence.
final_diagnosis: Fa0/2 is assigned to VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 10, causing Layer 2 connectivity failure.

root_cause: VLAN 20 is missing from the allowed VLAN list on the trunk interface connecting SW1 and SW2.
evidence: show interfaces trunk output indicates VLAN 20 is not in the allowed VLAN list.
fix_steps: Enter interface configuration mode for the trunk interface on the switch using 'interface <interface_name>'. | Add VLAN 20 to the trunk allowed VLAN list using 'switchport trunk allowed vlan add 20'. | Repeat the process on the connecting trunk interface of the neighbor switch if configured identically. | Verify connectivity between hosts in VLAN 20 using ping.
additional_evidence_needed: Running configuration of the trunk interfaces on both switches to confirm both sides require updating.
risk: Low. Using 'switchport trunk allowed vlan add 20' appends the VLAN to the existing allowed list without disrupting existing allowed VLAN traffic.
expected_fault: VLAN 20 is missing from the trunk allowed list.
human_correction: Confirmed VLAN 20 must be allowed on the trunk interface.
reason_for_correction: Compared AI diagnosis with the documented expected fault and trunk evidence.
final_diagnosis: VLAN 20 is missing from the trunk allowed VLAN list, preventing VLAN 20 traffic from crossing the trunk.

root_cause: Absence of a Layer 3 inter-VLAN routing mechanism (SVI or router-on-a-stick) to route traffic between distinct VLANs.
evidence: show vlan brief demonstrates that VLANs exist | show ip route demonstrates no routes or SVIs exist for the VLANs
fix_steps: Deploy a Layer 3 routing device or enable L3 features on the switch if supported. | Create SVI interfaces for each VLAN and assign appropriate IP addresses. | Enable IP routing using the 'ip routing' command if using an L3 switch. | Ensure hosts in each VLAN have their default gateway set to the corresponding SVI or router interface IP address.
additional_evidence_needed: Information on whether the switch supports Layer 3 routing or if an external router is connected via a trunk interface.
risk: Low risk when creating new SVIs and enabling IP routing.
human_correction: Confirmed that inter-VLAN routing is missing between VLAN 10 and VLAN 20.
reason_for_correction: Compared AI diagnosis with the documented expected fault and Layer 3 evidence.
final_diagnosis: No Layer 3 inter-VLAN routing mechanism is configured to route traffic between VLAN 10 and VLAN 20.

root_cause: Native VLAN configuration mismatch across the EtherChannel trunk interface causing STP inconsistency or port down state.
evidence: show etherchannel summary shows Port-channel is down | show interfaces trunk shows native VLAN mismatch
fix_steps: Access configuration mode on both switch peers for the relevant Port-channel interface. | Execute 'switchport trunk native vlan 150' on both sides to align the native VLAN configuration. | Verify port-channel recovery using 'show etherchannel summary' and 'show interfaces trunk'.
additional_evidence_needed: Running configuration of the Port-channel and member physical interfaces on both switches.
risk: Modifying trunk interface settings may cause a brief disruption in network traffic while the link re-converges.
expected_fault: Native VLAN configuration is inconsistent on the Port-channel/trunk.
human_correction: Confirmed the native VLAN must match on both sides of the EtherChannel trunk.
reason_for_correction: Compared AI diagnosis with the documented expected fault and EtherChannel/trunk evidence.
final_diagnosis: The EtherChannel trunk has a native VLAN mismatch between the two switch peers.

root_cause: The PC is configured with an incorrect default gateway IP address (192.168.10.254) instead of the actual router gateway interface address (192.168.10.1).
evidence: PC IP configuration gateway is set to 192.168.10.254 | Router interface IP address is 192.168.10.1
fix_steps: Change the default gateway configuration on the PC to 192.168.10.1. | Test reachability from the PC to the remote network using ping.
additional_evidence_needed: None, the available evidence directly confirms the IP configuration mismatch between the PC default gateway and the router interface.
expected_fault: PC has the wrong default gateway.
human_correction: Confirmed the PC default gateway must be changed to 192.168.10.1.
reason_for_correction: Compared AI diagnosis with the documented expected fault and router interface evidence.
final_diagnosis: The PC is configured with an incorrect default gateway of 192.168.10.254 instead of 192.168.10.1.

root_cause: Incorrect host subnet mask configured on the PC, causing remote traffic to be misclassified as local or improperly routed instead of being forwarded to the default gateway.
evidence: Router LAN interface is 192.168.20.1/24 | PC default gateway is set to 192.168.20.1 | PC can ping local devices but cannot reach remote subnets
fix_steps: Reconfigure the PC subnet mask to match the network mask of 255.255.255.0 (/24). | Confirm the PC default gateway is correctly set to 192.168.20.1. | Verify connectivity from the PC to remote subnets via ping.
additional_evidence_needed: Host IP configuration details (e.g., ipconfig /all output) to confirm the configured subnet mask on the PC.
risk: Low; updating local PC subnet mask settings affects network configuration on the individual host only.
expected_fault: Incorrect host subnet mask prevents correct remote-network forwarding.

root_cause: The client PC has no DNS server IP address configured in its IP settings, preventing hostname resolution while direct IP connectivity remains functional.
evidence: Web server opens by IP address but not by hostname. | PC IP configuration shows the DNS server field is blank.
fix_steps: Configure the DNS server option under the appropriate DHCP pool on the router using the 'dns-server <IP-address>' command. | If statically assigned, manually enter the primary DNS server IP address in the client PC network adapter settings. | Execute 'ipconfig /renew' on the client PC to obtain updated DNS server settings from DHCP.
additional_evidence_needed: DHCP pool configuration from the Cisco device to confirm whether DNS server options are configured for lease distribution.
expected_fault: Client has no DNS server configured.

root_cause: An Access Control List (ACL) entry applied to the router is blocking DNS and HTTP traffic.
evidence: DNS and HTTP fail after an ACL is applied. | show access-lists shows DNS/HTTP traffic is denied by an ACL entry.
fix_steps: Modify the ACL to explicitly permit DNS (UDP/TCP port 53) and HTTP (TCP port 80) traffic from internal clients to destination services. | Apply the updated ACL configuration to the active interface.
additional_evidence_needed: Output of 'show ip interface' to confirm interface assignment and direction of the applied ACL.
risk: Modifying Access Control Lists may lead to unintended network outages or security exposure if rules are configured incorrectly.
